title: A Visitor for the Portrait
premise: Quentin Oyelaran's late-night radio show has an audience that shouldn't exist: callers describing their own deaths from the week before. When an excavation crew beneath the old Aldercrest theater unearths a door sealed from the inside, the dead callers' voices begin arriving through the station's equipment, each humming the same incomplete song. Quentin discovers the door is a mouth, and the song's missing last verse is an invitation — sung correctly, it opens the way in; sung along with, it opens the way out for what's inside. To protect the city, Quentin must learn the verse from the dead without ever singing a note himself, and in the final broadcast he performs the verse silently, mouthing the words as the door devours his voice instead of the town, leaving him a host with no sound, remembered only by listeners who can no longer hear him.
about_author: Wren Vasquez is a former overnight radio producer who swears every station has one dead frequency. They write horror in the hours when the phones ring and nobody is on the line.

chapters.title: Dead Air, Warm Voices
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. During his 2 a.m. show, a caller named Marisol describes her own drowning six days ago, in detail no one could know. Quentin keeps his composure on air, then checks the obituaries and confirms it. Emotional beat: quiet dread — the professional mask holding over a crack of terror.

chapters.title: The Count of Doors
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. His rituals — lights on, doors counted, salt lines — are revealed as inherited from his grandmother, a radio operator who vanished in 1974. A second dead caller, a construction worker, mentions 'the door under Aldercrest.' Emotional beat: the comfort of routine curdling into the knowledge that routine was always a ward.

chapters.title: What the Excavator Found
chapters.summary: POV Nadia, the excavation forewoman. Her crew breaks a wall beneath the condemned theater and finds a door with hinges on the inside, warm to the touch, sealed from within. That night her crew members begin humming a tune none of them know. Emotional beat: hubris and unease — they think they've found history.

chapters.title: Caller on Line Two
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. A caller hums the tune, and the station's dead equipment lights up. Marisol returns, warning: 'Don't learn the last verse. It's learning you.' Quentin traces the melody to a 1938 broadcast from Aldercrest that was never aired. Emotional beat: fascination warring with self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Verse That Isn't There
chapters.summary: POV Nadia. Two crew members go missing; the remaining ones can't stop humming, and the humming is harmonizing with something below. Nadia finds the 1938 station log in the theater archive: the last verse was cut from the recording on purpose, by an engineer who then sealed himself in. Emotional beat: desperation — knowledge arriving too fast.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Kind of Lure
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. His producer Dev, his only friend, starts singing in his sleep and defends the door's 'generosity' — it grants the dead one more conversation. Quentin realizes the entity buys loyalty with memory, showing Dev his dead mother's voice. Emotional beat: heartbreak — the truth may cost him the person he loves most.

chapters.title: Inside the Hinge
chapters.summary: POV Nadia. She descends alone and touches the door; through it she hears every missing person, alive and singing, and glimpses the engineer's skeleton at a console, mouth open mid-note. She understands: the song never ends because the singers can't stop. Emotional beat: horror as revelation — the door is a choir being kept.

chapters.title: The Last Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. The entity hijacks the station's frequency citywide, and everyone who has heard the song begins singing the first three verses in the streets. Dev begs him to sing along and be reunited with the dead. Emotional beat: climax — loyalty and truth pulling Quentin apart on live air.

chapters.title: Mouthed, Not Sung
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. He reconstructs the final verse from Marisol's fragments and the engineer's log, and performs it silently — lips moving, throat closed, voice offered without song. The door takes his voice instead of the city; the singing stops mid-note; the frequency goes dead. Emotional beat: sacrifice — truth kept by refusing the one act of joining.

chapters.title: A Visitor for the Portrait
chapters.summary: POV Nadia, weeks later. The town is quiet; Dev doesn't remember Quentin, and neither do the tapes — except one portrait of Quentin in the studio that Nadia swears watches her. Each night, the dead frequency plays three seconds of silence shaped like a man. Emotional beat: mournful resolution — memory as the only grave a silenced man gets.
